incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sudden spike in OOMs on prod-serving-1 prefills (prefill path). 120 container restarts in last 10m. Autoscaler triggered node drains.

maya (oncall): seeing the alerts, joining bridge. paging sam and rachel.

sam: on it, grabbing logs. which model(s) affected?

jordan: looks like multi-model impact but concentrated on large-context models (gptx-32k variants).

lee (sre): quick kubectl snapshot: `kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=prefill -o wide` shows high RESTARTS for pods on node gpu-12. node gpu-12 mem pressure 94%.

rachel (ml-runtime): log snippet from one container: ```[2026-03-17T02:12:33Z] runtime.cpp:cuda_call: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY while allocating 1048576000 bytes
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
containerd: shim reaped pid 12345 
```

maya (oncall): customer-ops, any customer impact reported?

customer-ops: we have 2 customers with elevated 5xx: Acme (support ticket #4532) and GammaLabs via webhook failures. Both started ~02:10 UTC. Acme's SLA-sensitive routes hit ~30% errors.

sam: reproducing locally with a 28k prompt prefilling full KV cache - memory climbs then process OOMs. Prefill is doing full attention state allocation.

rachel (ml-runtime): root cause hypothesis: long-context prefill allocate full KV caches concurrently for large batch sizes. sudden traffic spike + large prompts -> eviction can't keep up -> OOMs. Also seeing CUDA memory fragmentation warnings.

lee (sre): mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill token cap (runtime config) 2) reduce concurrency on affected nodes (scale down rt replicas) 3) route large-context requests to fallback smaller model or CPU fallback 4) cordon/evict node gpu-12 and let scheduler rebalance. Which do we want immediate?

maya (oncall): priority = customer impact. Let's do quick live mitigations: A) apply runtime cap to max_prefill_tokens=8192 -> prevents >8k prefill attempts. B) add routing rule to send requests >16k to fallback-quantized-16k (lower memory) C) cordon gpu-12 and drain gradually. Sam/rachel take A+B, lee handle C.

sam: applying runtime change now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/runtime/config -d '{"max_prefill_tokens":8192}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSKEY'` -> response 200. Rolling restart of runtime proxies 3/3 successful.

rachel (ml-runtime): pushed routing tweak to edge rules: `if request.context_tokens > 16000 -> model=fallback-quant-16k` deployed to 4 regions. Confirming warmups started.

sam: monitoring memory and restarts... initial signal: container restarts dropped from 120->18 in next 5m.

lee (sre): cordoning node gpu-12 and draining pods now: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> drain in progress, some pods restarted on gpu-05 and gpu-07. No new node-level OOMs yet.

customer-ops: notifying Acme and GammaLabs: sent brief that we saw OOMs due to large-context prefill; mitigations applied and traffic routed to fallback models; ETA to full remediation 30-60m.

maya (oncall): what's health dashboard showing?

sam: metrics: prefill_oom_rate peaked at 0.35 then down to 0.02. average p95 latency for generation increased ~120ms due to fallback routing. Error budget burn reduced.

rachel (ml-runtime): follow-up plan: 1) add runtime-level fine-grained token prefill accounting to refuse atomic prefill > X per-request 2) add best-effort prefill streaming to avoid full-KV allocation 3) better fragmentation mitigation (cudaMalloc defrag) 4) test quantized fallback perf for heavy traffic.

lee (sre): infra follow-ups: add alert that correlates concurrent prefill allocations + node mem fragmentation; add automation to limit concurrency per-node for large-context models.

maya (oncall): customers updated at 02:45 UTC, ops ticket created. Who's owning postmortem?

sam: I'll own the triage write-up (root cause + quick mitigations). rachel will own runtime changes and tests. lee will own infra alerts and node-level automation. maya will coordinate customer comms and severity.

customer-ops: Acme confirms degraded but accepting routed fallback for now. GammaLabs reports some truncated outputs but no data loss.

maya (oncall): status -> mitigated. Will keep bridge open for 45m for follow-ups. If anything new, ping @maya. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: severity=high, status=mitigated, runbook=long-prefill-oom. Logs and metrics archived to incident-1767754321.

sam: posting a short remediation diff in #eng-runtime once postmortem started.

rachel (ml-runtime): quick note: need to add a policy to the router that limits simultaneous prefill allocations per model across replicas. Currently on our backlog.

lee (sre): final check: memory pressure back to normal 52% on previously impacted nodes. No further restarts in last 10m.

maya (oncall): thanks team. closing live mitigation. follow-ups tracked in GH issue #9876.
